Description:
A rod standing in the hole of a torus, exactly as wide as the hole: the two surfaces touch along a WHOLE
CIRCLE and nowhere else. Of the three kinds of tangential contact this is the one that is not a point -
Surfaces.ContactType calls it Degenerate - and it is the hardest to get right, because the two surfaces
osculate along the contact and the intersection curve is not a curve of transversal crossing anywhere.

  nurbsTorus  R = 18, r = 8 about the z axis, so its inner equator is the circle rho = 10, z = 0.
              solid.sweep of an exact NURBS circle along an exact NURBS circle, so the mantle is a
              SweptCurveSurface, not a ToroidalSurface.
  nurbsRod    r = 10 about the z axis, z from -20 to 20. solid.extrude of an exact NURBS circle, so the
              mantle is a SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion, not a CylindricalSurface.

The rod's mantle rho = 10 and the torus' inner equator rho = 10, z = 0 meet in that whole circle, and
there the two surfaces have the same tangent plane - the torus' normal at the inner equator is radial
and horizontal, which is the rod's normal as well. The rod deliberately reaches from z = -20 to z = 20,
far past the tube's |z| <= 8, so the contact circle lies in the INTERIOR of the rod's mantle and is not
mixed up with a cap.

The two solids therefore have disjoint interiors and touch along a curve. That makes three of the four
operations trivial in substance and hard in execution, which is the point: a boolean operation that does
not recognize the contact will either lose the touching circle or invent an intersection body from it.
Expected:
Two closed solids, and results that are pinned exactly because the interiors are disjoint.

  nurbsTorus  V = 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 2*pi^2*18*64 = 22739.5685401099
              A = 4*pi^2*R*r = 4*pi^2*144 = 5684.8921350275
              extent -26, -26, -8 .. 26, 26, 8, no cap at all - the path closes
  nurbsRod    V = pi*10^2*40 = 12566.3706143592
              A = 2*pi*10*40 + 2*pi*100 = 3141.5926535898
              extent -10, -10, -20 .. 10, 10, 20

  torusRodInter   EMPTY. The interiors are disjoint - the whole tube has rho >= 10 and the rod has
                  rho <= 10 - so the intersection is the contact circle, which has no volume. The
                  operation must report an empty result and store nothing under the name, recorded as
                  { "exists": "false" }. Returning a body here, of any size, is the failure this case
                  is watching for.
  torusRodUnion   V = 22739.5685401099 + 12566.3706143592 = 35305.9391544691
                  A = 5684.8921350275 + 3141.5926535898 = 8826.4847886173
                  extent -26, -26, -20 .. 26, 26, 20
                  The two bodies meet only along a circle, so the union is NOT a manifold solid. Whether
                  the operation answers with one non manifold solid or with the two operands side by
                  side is its own decision; what is binding is that no material is added or lost.
  torusMinusRod   the torus, unchanged: V = 22739.5685401099, A = 5684.8921350275
  rodMinusTorus   the rod, unchanged:   V = 12566.3706143592, A = 3141.5926535898

Both differences have to come back with the operand's own numbers to the last digit. A difference that
subtracts anything at all has misread the tangential contact as an overlap, and one that returns nothing
has misread it as containment - the two failure modes this arrangement separates.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
OK since 2026-09-20. The case was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-09-17, when ALL FOUR operations threw -
"Error in the application." for the union and rodMinusTorus, "Constructing Polyline2D with less than two
points" for the intersection and torusMinusRod - so nothing was stored under any of the four names. It
was the last of the three tangential cases to come green, after ConesTangentAtMantlePoint had already
moved: the contact here is not a point but a WHOLE CIRCLE, the Degenerate case, where the two surfaces
osculate and the intersection curve crosses transversally nowhere.

WHAT IT PRODUCES NOW, and every one of the four is exactly what the Expected section demands - which is
unusually sharp here, because the interiors are disjoint and the answers are therefore known without any
computation:
  torusRodInter   EMPTY, recorded as { "exists": "false" }. Returning a body of any size here would mean
                  the contact circle was mistaken for an overlap, and that is the failure this
                  arrangement exists to catch.
  torusMinusRod   the torus back, UNCHANGED: 22739.5684875, area 5684.89212186, edgeLength
                  316.989109996, extent and the SweptCurveSurface:4 histogram all identical to the
                  nurbsTorus operand to the last recorded digit.
  rodMinusTorus   the rod back, UNCHANGED, identical to the nurbsRod operand in every field.
  torusRodUnion   TWO solids of 22739.5684875 and 12566.3705834, which are the two operands side by
                  side. Their volumes sum to 35305.9390709 against the exact 35305.9391544691 and their
                  areas to 8826.48476616 against the exact 8826.4847886173, both 2.5e-09 - so nothing
                  was added and nothing was lost, which is the binding requirement.

WHY THE UNION IS NOT ASSERTED. The two bodies meet along a circle, so their union is not a manifold
solid, and the Expected section deliberately leaves it open whether the operation answers with one non
manifold solid or with the two operands side by side. It currently does the latter. Pinning "two solids"
in an assert.check would contradict that, so the partition is left to the baseline: should the operation
start joining them, the case goes red and the new answer is judged against the sum, not rejected.
The two DIFFERENCES are asserted (calls 15 to 18), because there the answer is not a matter of taste -
each one has to give its operand back - and they are read with Solid.Volume, which does not depend on
the recorded fingerprint.

Unlike NurbsConesTangentAtMantlePoint this case needs no warning about its recorded numbers. Nothing
here is a trimmed planar face: the torus has no lid at all and the rod's two lids keep their full
circular outline of radius 10, which is one of the radii where Border.Area is exact. Volume and area are
therefore the geometry, and they meet the calculated values to 2.5e-09.
